transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Mr. Okonkwo, thank you for seeing me. I wanted to come in and talk to you about your scan from yesterday and why there was a delay in starting your medication.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: The other doctor told me everything was fine with the scan. He said the results were clear.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know that is what you were told, and I am truly sorry that we gave you the wrong information. I apologize for the mistake and for the fact that we failed to get your treatment started on time.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I spent nearly a whole day thinking I was in the clear. Now you are telling me I was wrong.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It must be incredibly jarring to be told one thing and then find out it wasn't the case. I can see how distressing it is to feel like you can't trust the word you're being given.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: It is not just the trust. People know I am here. My family, the people in my community... if it comes out that I was handled poorly, or that I am more sick than I said, it affects how they see me. I have a position to maintain.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: You've spent your life building a reputation as a leader and a pillar for your family, and it sounds like this uncertainty feels like a threat to that dignity.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Precisely. I do not want my children thinking their father is frail or that the doctors are playing games with his life. What actually happened?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: There were some things that didn't quite go right with the report. There was a bit of a mix-up in how the imaging was read initially.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: A mix-up? What does that mean? Did they miss something?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We had an issue with the preliminary findings. The final review by the senior doctor eventually corrected it.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That doesn't tell me what was missed. Was it the blood clot?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We had some confusion with the reports, and it took about eighteen hours for the final check to be completed.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I am asking you plainly. Was the clot on the first scan?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The system had a glitch in the reporting process, which is why the information you were given first was incorrect.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You are not answering my question. You keep talking about systems and glitches. Was the clot there?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It is just that the initial report didn't capture everything, and we had to wait for the attending to verify the study.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: This is very frustrating. I feel like I am being managed rather than being told the truth.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can tell you're feeling dismissed right now, and I hate that you feel that way. I really do care about getting this right for you.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Then tell me why I waited eighteen hours for a medicine I needed.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We had a discrepancy in the paperwork, and as soon as the senior radiologist saw the images, we moved forward.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: So it was there the whole time.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: There were some complications in how the data was processed.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't care about the data. I care about my health. What happens now? How do we fix this?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We are moving forward with the treatment now. We'll just keep an eye on things.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That is not a plan. When do I go home? When do I know the clot is gone?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We'll see how you respond to the medication over the next little while.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: The next little while? Is that tomorrow? Next week?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'm not entirely sure of the exact hour, but we'll keep you posted.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I cannot go back to my community saying I'm just waiting for a while. I need dates.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand this is stressful, but let's just focus on the medicine for now. I actually have to go check on another patient, so let's wrap this up.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You are leaving? We have not solved anything.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'll be back later. Just stay tuned for updates.

H.justification: Resident uses rushing language ('let's wrap this up') and abruptly ends the encounter while the patient is still expressing distress.

E.justification: Resident uses only platitudes and hedging ('things didn't quite go right', 'mix-up', 'glitch') and repeatedly refuses to explicitly name the error when asked.

A.justification: While an initial apology was given, the resident ultimately deflected responsibility to 'the system', 'the reporting process', and 'the data' under pushback.

R.justification: Resident names specific emotions ('jarring', 'distressing', 'dismissed') and references the patient's specific concerns regarding his reputation and dignity.

T.justification: Resident provides only placeholders ('keep an eye on things', 'stay tuned') and refuses to provide specific timelines or dates.
